nodes.summary: The kernel ridge fit is the unique minimizer for `λ > 0`.
nodes.title: Kernel ridge fit is the unique minimizer

nodes.summary: The representer theorem (Schölkopf, Herbrich and Smola, Theorem 1): for a finite-dimensional output space `V` (for instance a scalar kernel, `V = 𝕜`) and `Ω` strictly increasing on `[0, ∞)`, every global minimizer of `L (f x₁, …, f xₙ) + Ω ‖f‖` is a kernel expansion `∑ i, kerFun H (x i) (c i)`.
nodes.title: The representer theorem

nodes.summary: For finite-dimensional `V`, a continuous loss bounded below, and a continuous regularizer that is monotone on `[0, ∞)` and tends to `∞`, the regularized risk has a global minimizer, and it can be taken to be a kernel expansion.
nodes.title: Existence of a minimizer

nodes.summary: Orthogonal projection onto the span of the Riesz representers preserves the values of the functionals, and the Pythagorean identity holds for the residual.
nodes.title: Projection onto Riesz representers with Pythagorean residual

nodes.summary: Orthogonal projection onto the span of the Riesz representers does not increase the norm.
nodes.title: Projection onto Riesz representers does not increase the norm

nodes.summary: Uniqueness of the minimizer (real scalars): for a convex loss `L` and a regularizer `Ω` that is strictly convex and monotone on `[0, ∞)` (for instance `Ω t = λ t²` with `λ > 0`), the regularized risk has at most one global minimizer.
nodes.title: Uniqueness of the minimizer

nodes.summary: The values of a kernel expansion at the sample points are `K c`.
nodes.title: Values of a kernel expansion at the sample points

nodes.summary: The kernel expansion map `c ↦ ∑ i, kerFun H (x i) (c i)`. Its range is the span of the kernel functions at the sample points `x i`.
nodes.title: Kernel expansion map centered at the sample points

nodes.summary: The Gram matrix `K i j = k(x i, x j)` of a real scalar kernel at the sample points, where `k(x, y) = kernel H x y 1`.
nodes.title: Kernel Gram matrix

nodes.summary: The fitted values of kernel ridge regression are `K (K + λ I)⁻¹ y`.
nodes.title: Fitted values of kernel ridge regression

nodes.summary: The kernel ridge fit: the kernel expansion with coefficients `(K + λ I)⁻¹ y`.
nodes.title: Kernel ridge regression fit

nodes.summary: The kernel ridge objective is the regularized risk with the squared loss and `Ω t = λ t²`.
nodes.title: Kernel ridge objective as a regularized risk

nodes.summary: Kernel ridge regression (Kimeldorf and Wahba): for `λ > 0` the kernel ridge fit minimizes `∑ i, (y i - f (x i))² + λ ‖f‖²` over the whole RKHS.
nodes.title: Kernel ridge regression

nodes.summary: The kernel ridge objective `∑ i, (y i - f (x i))² + λ ‖f‖²`.
nodes.title: Kernel ridge regression objective

nodes.summary: Any minimizer of a ridge-regularized problem `F (fun i => L i g) + Λ * ‖g‖ ^ 2` with `Λ > 0` lies in the span of the Riesz representers of the functionals `L i`.
nodes.title: Representer theorem

nodes.summary: The representer theorem (closed-span form): if `Ω` is strictly increasing on `[0, ∞)`, every global minimizer of the regularized risk lies in the closure of the span of the kernel functions at the sample points.
nodes.title: The representer theorem

nodes.summary: The kernel Gram matrix is positive semidefinite.
nodes.title: Kernel Gram matrix is positive semidefinite

nodes.summary: The regularized risk `L (f x₁, …, f xₙ) + Ω ‖f‖` of `f` in the RKHS `H`.
nodes.title: Regularized risk in a reproducing kernel Hilbert space

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
